name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operative pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by Wisconsin Statutes §340.01(15ph) and regulated by §346.806, both created by 2019 Wisconsin Act 34.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 may be powered by the motor alone but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Fully operative pedals and a motor of 750 watts or less
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512), and the motor stops providing power when the brakes are applied or the rider stops pedaling
A Class 3 must have a speedometer that reasonably accurately shows its speed in miles per hour
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point Arial stating its class, the speed at which the motor stops assisting, and motor wattage
Anyone who modifies it so its class changes must affix a revised label to match
Riders under 16 may not ride a Class 3, but may ride as a passenger on one designed to carry passengers
Has a bicycle's rights and duties, and is a vehicle to the same extent as a bicycle
May be ridden with the motor on along bikeways, but a municipality or county may ban that by ordinance, and the Department of Natural Resources by rule, on bikeways it controls
Not a motor vehicle or motor bicycle: no operator's license, registration, title or insurance
